info.name: Social Media Feed App
info.description:
REST API for the Social Media Feed App (Week 5).

## Authentication
Auth uses a **JWT stored in an httpOnly cookie** named `token`. The token is never returned in the response body. Postman stores the cookie after **Login** and sends it automatically with later requests, the same way a browser does.

## How to use
1. Set `baseUrl`, in the collection **Variables** tab:
   - Local: `http://localhost:5000/api`
   - Live: `https://social-feed-api.vercel.app/api`
2. Run the requests in order (top to bottom), or use **Run collection**. Every request has tests that check the status code and response shape.
3. **Register** generates a fresh email each run and saves it in `testEmail`, so the whole collection can be re-run without duplicate-email failures. The fixed demo account for manual testing is `test@example.com` / `password123`.

## Response format
Success: `{ "success": true, ... }`

Error: `{ "success": false, "message": "...", "errors": { "field": "message" } }`. `errors` is only present on validation failures.

## Status codes
| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | OK |
| 201 | Created (register) |
| 400 | Validation failed / invalid JSON |
| 401 | Not authenticated, invalid or expired token, wrong credentials |
| 403 | Not the owner of the post |
| 404 | Route or post not found |
| 409 | Email already registered |
| 503 | Health check: database disconnected |

item.name: Health

request.description:
Checks that the server is running and connected to MongoDB.

- **200**: `status: "ok"`, `database: "connected"`
- **503**: `status: "degraded"`, the server is up but the database is disconnected

Also returns `uptime` (seconds) and `timestamp`. Public, no auth needed. On the live Vercel URL the first request after idle time can take a few seconds (cold start).

request.description:
Creates a new user account.

**Body**
| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| `name` | Required, 2-50 characters, trimmed |
| `email` | Required, valid email, stored lowercased, must be unique |
| `password` | Required, 8-72 characters, at least one letter and one number |

Only these three fields are saved. Extra fields like `role` are ignored. The password is hashed with bcrypt before it is stored and is never returned.

**Responses**
- **201**: `Registration successful` plus the user object (`id`, `name`, `email`, `avatar`, `bio`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`)
- **400**: validation errors, per field
- **409**: `Email is already registered`

The pre-request script generates a unique email each run and saves it for the Login request.

exec: pm.test("Returns an error for every invalid field", () => {

request.description:
Registers again with the email from the Register request. Run Register first.

**Expected (409)**: `Email is already registered`

Correct email, wrong password.

**Expected (401)**: `Invalid email or password`. No cookie is set.

request.description:
Email that is not registered.

**Expected (401)**: exactly the same response as a wrong password. The API doesn't reveal whether the email exists, which protects against user enumeration.

exec: pm.test("Returns the user without password or token", () => {

request.description:
Logs in with email and password.

**Body**: `email` and `password`, both required.

**Responses**
- **200**: `Login successful` plus the user object. A `token` cookie is set with `HttpOnly`, a 7-day `Max-Age`, and `SameSite=Lax` locally or `SameSite=None; Secure` in production.
- **400**: missing fields
- **401**: `Invalid email or password`, the same message whether the email or the password is wrong

The JWT is **only** in the cookie, never in the body, so frontend JavaScript can't read it (XSS protection). Postman saves the cookie and sends it with the next requests.

To log in with the demo account instead, change the body to `test@example.com` / `password123`.

🔒 **Protected.** Returns the currently authenticated user. The frontend calls this on page load to restore the session.

The `protect` middleware reads the `token` cookie, verifies the JWT signature and expiry, and loads the user from the database.

**Responses**
- **200**: `{ success: true, user }`
- **401**: one of:
  - `Not authenticated. Please log in.`: no cookie
  - `Invalid token. Please log in again.`: tampered or malformed token
  - `Session expired. Please log in again.`: token past its 7-day expiry
  - `User no longer exists. Please log in again.`: account was deleted

Run **Login** first.

Logs out by clearing the `token` cookie. It sends back an expired cookie with the same options it was set with, so the browser deletes it.

**Not protected on purpose:** logout must still work when the token has already expired. Otherwise the stale cookie would stay in the browser.

**Response (200)**: `Logged out successfully`

It uses `POST`, not `GET`, so that links, image tags, or browser prefetching can't log a user out.

Same as **Me**, but run after **Logout** to confirm the session has ended.

**Expected (401)**: `Not authenticated. Please log in.`

item.description:
Registration, login, logout, and session check.

Auth is a JWT in an httpOnly cookie named `token`, valid for 7 days. Requests marked 🔒 need a valid cookie, so run **Login** first.

item.name: Users

exec: // This folder runs after Logout, so log in again to get a fresh cookie.

request.description:
🔒 **Protected.** Returns the logged-in user's profile for the Profile page: `id`, `name`, `email`, `avatar`, `bio`, `createdAt` (join date), and `updatedAt`.

**How it differs from `/auth/me`:** `/auth/me` answers "who is logged in?" for the session check. `/users/me` is the profile resource. Profile editing (`PATCH /users/me`) and public profiles (`GET /users/:id`) will be added here later.

**Responses**
- **200**: `{ success: true, user }`
- **401**: not authenticated

The pre-request script logs in first, because this runs after Logout in the collection order.

item.name: Posts
item.description:
Create, read, update, and delete posts, and read the feed. 🔒 Every request needs a logged-in user. The folder's pre-request script logs in with `testEmail` (set by Auth → Register) and falls back to the demo account.

Update and delete are owner-only. See **Posts - Ownership** for the 403 cases.

exec: // Log in before each request in this folder, so it works after Auth → Logout
// and when the folder is run on its own.
pm.test("Returns the post with basic author info only", () => {
pm.test("Content is trimmed", () => pm.expect(post.content).to.eql("Working on my new project today!"));

request.description:
🔒 Creates a post for the logged-in user.

**Body**
| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| `content` | Required, text, trimmed, 1–500 characters |
| `imageUrl` | Optional, must be an `https://` URL. Empty or missing means no image. |

The author always comes from the session, never from the body. Extra fields like `author` or `likesCount` are ignored.

**Responses**
- **201**: `Post created` plus the post, with `author: { id, name, avatar }`
- **400**: validation errors
- **401**: not logged in

Saves the new post's id in `postId` for later requests.
🔒 Same as Create Post, with the optional `imageUrl`.

exec: pm.test("Authors expose only id, name, avatar", () => {

request.description:
🔒 The social feed: all posts, newest first. Defaults to `page=1`, `limit=10`.

Each post includes `author: { id, name, avatar }` only, with no email or other private fields.

**Response (200)**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "posts": [ ... ],
  "pagination": { "page": 1, "limit": 10, "total": 42, "totalPages": 5, "hasMore": true }
}
```
The frontend uses `hasMore` to decide whether to show "Load more".

🔒 Pagination with query params. `page` starts at 1. `limit` is 1–50.

`skip = (page - 1) * limit`. Posts are sorted by `createdAt` then `_id` (both descending), so the order is stable and a post never appears on two pages.

🔒 `page` must be ≥ 1 and `limit` 1–50. The cap stops clients from fetching every post in one request.

**Expected (400)**: errors for both `page` and `limit`.

exec: // Fetch the first 2 posts and use the last one as the cursor.
pm.test("Only posts older than the cursor", () => {

request.description:
🔒 **Cursor mode**, used by the frontend's Load more button. Returns posts older than the given post (`before` = its `createdAt`, `beforeId` = its `id`).

Unlike `?page=`, a cursor can't repeat or skip posts when posts are created or deleted between requests. Both params must be sent together.

**Response (200)**: `{ posts, pagination: { limit, hasMore } }`

exec: pm.test("Author has only id, name, avatar", () => pm.expect(post.author).to.have.all.keys("id", "name", "avatar"));

request.description:
🔒 Returns one post by id, with `author: { id, name, avatar }`.

**Responses**
- **200**: `{ success, post }`
- **400**: `Invalid post id` (not a MongoDB id)
- **404**: `Post not found`

Uses `postId` from Create Post.

exec: pm.test("Says the post was not found", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql("Post not found"));

request.description:

exec: pm.expect(post.content).to.eql("Edited: shipped the first version today!");
pm.test("updatedAt moved forward", () => pm.expect(new Date(post.updatedAt) > new Date(post.createdAt)).to.eql(true));

request.description:
🔒 **Owner only.** Updates `content` and/or `imageUrl`. Only the fields you send are changed. Send `imageUrl: ""` to remove the image.

Same rules as Create Post, and at least one of the two fields is required.

**Responses**
- **200**: `Post updated` plus the updated post (`updatedAt` changes)
- **400**: validation errors, or `errors.body = "Nothing to update"`
- **403**: `You can only modify your own posts`
- **404**: `Post not found`

exec: pm.expect(post.content).to.eql("Edited: shipped the first version today!");

request.description: 🔒 Sends only `imageUrl: ""`. The image is removed and the content stays the same.

🔒 An empty body has nothing to change.

**Expected (400)**: `errors.body = "Nothing to update"`

exec: pm.test("Rejects empty content", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().errors.content).to.eql("Post content cannot be empty"));

request.description:
🔒 If `content` is sent, it can't be empty.

**Expected (400)**: `Post content cannot be empty`

🔒 **Owner only.** Permanently deletes the post.

**Responses**
- **200**: `{ success: true, message: "Post deleted", id }`. The frontend uses `id` to remove the card.
- **403**: `You can only modify your own posts`
- **404**: `Post not found`

exec: pm.test("Says the post was not found", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql("Post not found"));

request.description:
🔒 Deleting the same post again.

**Expected (404)**: `Post not found`

item.name: Posts - Ownership
item.description:
Proves users can't edit or delete other users' posts. The requests run in order:

1. Register a second user (`otherEmail`)
2. Log in as that user
3. Create a post as that user (`otherPostId`)
4. Log back in as the main user
5. Try to edit and delete the other user's post. Both return **403**.

request.description: Creates a second account with a fresh email for the ownership tests.
Sets the auth cookie for the second user.
Creates a post owned by the second user and saves its id in `otherPostId`.
Switches the cookie back to the main user (`testEmail`, or the demo account if Register wasn't run).

exec: pm.test("Explains why", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql("You can only modify your own posts"));

request.description:
🔒 The main user tries to edit the second user's post.

**Expected (403)**: `You can only modify your own posts`. The post is unchanged.

exec: pm.test("Explains why", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql("You can only modify your own posts"));

request.description:
🔒 The main user tries to delete the second user's post.

**Expected (403)**: `You can only modify your own posts`. The post still exists.

exec: pm.test("Content unchanged", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().post.content).to.eql("This post belongs to another user"));

request.description: 🔒 Confirms the forbidden edit and delete didn't change anything.
